topicName: Advanced SQL Queries (Joins, Subqueries, Analytical Functions)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced SQL Queries in Oracle DB"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covers advanced SQL query techniques in Oracle Database, including joins, subqueries, and analytical functions. These techniques are essential for extracting meaningful insights from complex datasets."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Joins"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Joins are used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column. Oracle supports several types of joins:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"INNER JOIN: Returns rows only when there is a match in both tables."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LEFT (OUTER) JOIN: Returns all rows from the left table and the matching rows from the right table. If there is no match, NULL values are returned for the right table's columns."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"RIGHT (OUTER) JOIN: Returns all rows from the right table and the matching rows from the left table. If there is no match, NULL values are returned for the left table's columns."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"FULL (OUTER) JOIN: Returns all rows when there is a match in either the left or right table. If there is no match, NULL values are returned for the missing side."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CROSS JOIN: Returns the Cartesian product of the tables, meaning every row from the first table is combined with every row from the second table."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"-- Example: INNER JOIN
SELECT e.employee_id, e.employee_name, d.department_name
FROM employees e
INNER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id;"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"-- Example: LEFT JOIN
SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_name
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Subqueries"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"A subquery is a query nested inside another SQL query. Subqueries can be used in the SELECT, FROM, WHERE, and HAVING clauses. They are useful for filtering or calculating values based on the results of another query."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Single-row subqueries: Return only one row."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Multiple-row subqueries: Return more than one row."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Correlated subqueries: Refer to a column in the outer query."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"-- Example: Subquery in WHERE clause
SELECT employee_name, salary
FROM employees
WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"-- Example: Correlated subquery
SELECT employee_name, department_id
FROM employees e
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM departments d WHERE e.department_id = d.department_id AND d.location = 'New York');"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Analytical Functions"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Analytical functions (also known as window functions) compute values across a set of table rows that are related to the current row. They are used for tasks like calculating running totals, rankings, and moving averages."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"RANK(): Assigns a rank to each row within a partition based on the specified order."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DENSE_RANK(): Similar to RANK(), but assigns consecutive ranks without gaps."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ROW_NUMBER(): Assigns a unique sequential integer to each row within a partition."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LAG(): Accesses data from a previous row in the same result set."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LEAD(): Accesses data from a subsequent row in the same result set."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SUM() OVER(): Calculates a running total."},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"-- Example: RANK() function
SELECT employee_name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank
FROM employees;"},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"-- Example: SUM() OVER() function
SELECT order_date, sales_amount, SUM(sales_amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS running_total
FROM sales;"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"These advanced SQL techniques provide powerful tools for data analysis and reporting in Oracle databases. Understanding and applying them effectively can significantly improve your ability to extract valuable insights from your data."}]
